A1.justification: Despite retitling and substantial restructuring, both PDFs describe the same transformer-development study. The complete main texts and appendices, including figures, tables and equations, support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original transformer-training experiments, LLC and essential-dynamics analyses, and behavioral and structural measurements for language modeling and synthetic regression.

after.justification: V2 retains original transformer-training results and developmental analyses, and adds language-model results across training seeds in Appendix B.4.

M1.justification: V1's combined LLC and essential-dynamics methodology becomes LLC-based stage detection. V2 removes trajectory PCA, vertex detection, form reconstruction and their use to corroborate milestones (v1 Sections 3.2–3.3 and Appendix B). The transformer architectures and LLC/SGLD-based approach remain.

E1.justification: The Pile, continuous and discrete-task regression, synthetic-token probes, and extreme-input/task scenarios remain. V1's Brownian-motion simulation used as a trajectory-PCA control (Figure 11d) is removed, providing a limited reduction in evaluation-scenario coverage.

E2.justification: Removing the form analyses also removes their comparisons with raw principal components, the nearest-checkpoint network and baseline pattern frequencies (v1 Figures 15–16). The retained Hessian comparison still includes the trace and three leading eigenvalues (v1 Figure 25; v2 Figure B.4).

E3.justification: The reported language-training sample count changes from 10 million to 5 million (v1 Table 6; v2 Table 3), while steps and batch size remain unchanged. The SGLD dataset entry changes from 1m to 13m, although v2's accompanying prose still specifies 1 million. These are reported-setting revisions; they do not establish that the main experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 removes form-validation analyses, the Brownian-motion control, and the explicit threshold-relaxation analysis yielding regression substages (v1 Appendix D.1.4 and Table 5). It adds language-model robustness checks across seeds. Positional ablations, one-layer controls, distribution-shift tests and SGLD sensitivity analyses remain.

E5.justification: V1 reports one language-model training seed and five regression seeds. V2 adds five-seed language-model curves and displays individual runs for both settings (Appendix B.4). It also reports fewer SGLD chains for additional language runs, without specifying their count. Existing regression-chain standard-deviation reporting remains.

E6.justification: Stage-summary boundaries and loss/LLC deltas remain unchanged, but Figure 1a replaces the language-model LLC curve: approximately 135–180 in v1 versus 80–150 in v2; v2 Figure B.1 retains the earlier scale. V2 adds seed-dependent findings, including late-stage subdivisions in three of five language runs, and removes form and substage results. The reported Hessian finding changes from detecting two boundaries to one, despite retaining the plotted curves.

T1.justification: V1's formal definitions, lemmas and proofs concerning vertices and forms are removed. V2 adds a volume-asymptotic definition of the LLC, expands the existing free-energy formula to include local multiplicity, and revises the layer-normalization degeneracy argument to distinguish vanishing weights from vanishing biases (Sections 4–5; Appendix D.2.4).

C1.justification: The central contribution shifts from introducing two stage-discovery methods and geometric forms to an empirical investigation of the connection between degeneracy and transformer development. The five-stage findings remain, while claims about forms organizing a developmental landscape disappear from the abstract, introduction and closing discussion.

C2.justification: V2 replaces v1's macroscopic-universality conjecture with explicitly setting-dependent case studies, limits LLC detection to sufficiently large developmental changes, and emphasizes unresolved causality. Section 8 and Appendix D.2.6 expand qualifications concerning collapse mechanisms and the gap between Bayesian inference and gradient-based training. Form-based interpretations are removed.

D1.justification: The reproducibility specifications for ED disappear, including functional proxies, 5,000-checkpoint regression trajectories and smoothing schedules. V2 newly specifies evaluation-set sizes of 512 language samples and 2,048 regression samples, adds TPU timing information for language replications, and replaces the anonymous code link with a named GitHub repository address.

R1.justification: Research positioning shifts substantially toward singular learning theory and degeneracy-based empirical analysis. Much of the essential-dynamics and trajectory-geometry literature is removed, while discussion adds singular-model foundations, complexity changes, statistical induction heads and refined LLC work, including Chen et al. (2024), Edelman et al. (2024) and Wang et al. (2025).

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and discussion are extensively rewritten. Related work moves forward, training/LLC/stage identification receive separate sections, and the appendices are reorganized around the retained methodology. V2 also adds an appendix contents page and an author-contribution statement.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. Stage tables are incorporated into Figure 1, language-result plots are consolidated into Figure 4, and numerous ED displays are removed. V2 redraws the LLC illustration and adds free-energy and multiple-seed figures. The collapse panel added to Figure 5 reuses earlier appendix evidence.

improvement.justification: Clearer LLC exposition, stronger qualifications and additional language-model replications benefit the focused argument. However, removing ED loses an alternative source of corroboration, while v2 leaves its revised Figure 1a unreconciled with Figure B.1 and introduces conflicting SGLD dataset sizes in Table 1 and its accompanying text. These unresolved issues in the central evidence prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
